title: Component playground

native.label: Shadcn native
native.hint: Vendored from the registry and unedited.

changed.label: Locally changed
changed.hint: Vendored, then edited locally — see the local-edit comment in the component source.

custom.label: Custom
custom.hint: Built in this app on top of shared shadcn primitives; not itself a registry component.

description: A visual reference for the shared UI library. Use this page to review components in light and dark themes before shipping them in product flows.

button.title: Button
button.description: Buttons start an action or confirm a decision. Their color communicates priority; their size should follow the surrounding control density.

variants.title: Variants
variants.description: Use one primary action per area. Secondary, outline, and ghost styles reduce visual priority; destructive is reserved for irreversible actions.

sizes.title: Sizes
sizes.description: The default 36 px control is the product baseline. Compact sizes are for dense interfaces, while large is for prominent actions.

radius.title: Radius
radius.description: Radius is independent from color and size. Use full for a pill-shaped text button or combine it with an icon size to produce a perfect circle.

icons.title: With icons
icons.description: Icons clarify familiar actions. Text buttons declare icon placement with data-icon; icon-only buttons always need an accessible label.

states.title: States and layout
states.description: Disabled and loading buttons keep their layout stable. Full-width buttons are composed with the standard className prop.

api.title: API reference
api.description: Project-facing styling props. Native button and Base UI interaction props are forwarded unchanged.

default.label: Default
default.description: The primary action in a view or dialog.

secondary.label: Secondary
secondary.description: A supporting action with a soft surface.

outline.label: Outline
outline.description: A neutral action that remains clearly bounded.

elevated.label: Elevated
elevated.description: A raised surface action: white in light, inverted to near-white in dark.

ghost.label: Ghost
ghost.description: A quiet action for toolbars and compact surfaces.

link.label: Link
link.description: A low-emphasis button action presented as text.

radius.defaultDescription: The standard component radius used by existing product controls.
radius.fullDescription: A pill shape for prominent or compact standalone actions.
radius.iconDescription: Equal width and height plus full radius produces a true circle.

rows.size: Sets the control height and icon-only geometry.
rows.radius: Selects the corner geometry. Full creates a pill or a circle for icon-only sizes.
rows.disabled: Prevents interaction and applies the disabled state.
rows.className: Adds layout utilities such as w-full without changing the recipe.
rows.render: Base UI element substitution. For navigation, style a Link with buttonVariants instead.

combobox.title: Combobox
combobox.description: The base search-with-popup primitive beneath every business picker in the product — user select, customer select, country select. Shown here bare, with local data only: the business wrappers live on the Platform pages.

single.title: Single value
single.description: Two trigger shapes: an input that shows the chosen value as its text, and a button-style trigger with the search field moved inside the popup — for pickers whose trigger renders identity markup, not text.
single.inputTrigger: The input itself is the trigger: typing filters, choosing fills the field.
single.buttonTrigger: A button trigger with no chevron (showChevron={false}) plus a search field inside the popup. The popup anchors to the field, not the button.

chips.title: Multiple — chips in the field
chips.description: ComboboxChips renders the selected values as removable chips with an inline search caret. Backspace on an empty field drops the last chip.
chips.hint: Selection is a T[]; each chip renders through the render slot and removes via its own aria-label.

states.title: States
states.description: Disabled passes through to the field and its clear affordances; an empty result set is where ComboboxEmpty shows its message.

usage.title: Real usage
usage.description: Four patterns already live in the product. They share the primitive but differ in trigger shape, data source, and where the search field lives — the four shapes a new picker starts from.

serverSearch.title: Server-side search — UserSelect
serverSearch.description: The input lives inside the popup, items come from GET /users with debounce, and picking a row never fills the search box. This is the shape the playground trigger-with-popup stand mirrors.

countrySelect.title: Flag trigger — CountrySelect
countrySelect.description: The trigger is a button rendering a flag and dial code; search sits in the popup and matches a stitched search string (name, ISO code, dial code) via itemToStringLabel.

chipsMulti.title: Chips multi-select — UserMultiSelect
chipsMulti.description: ComboboxChips with multiple; filtering is delegated to the server (filter={null}), so the built-in contains never lies about an unloaded page.

customerSelect.title: Domain rows — CustomerSelect
customerSelect.description: Same recipe as UserSelect but rendering CustomerIdentity rows; shows the primitive composing with domain markup inside the list.

api.title: API reference
api.description: Root props that shape the product's usage. The parts (Input, Trigger, Content, List, Item) forward Base UI's props unchanged; local edits add showChevron, showClear, removeLabel and the exported ComboboxClear.

single.inputTrigger: Type to filter a local list; choosing fills the field. The chevron button opens the same popup.
single.buttonTrigger: The trigger can be any markup — here a plain button with an icon. Search lives in the popup.

chips.hint: Chips render from the value array; the caret stays at the end. Backspace on an empty field removes the last chip.

states.emptyHint: Open the popup to see the empty state — no items, one message.

rows.multiple: Turns the root into a multi-select and makes value an array.
rows.items: The option list. Objects, not bare strings — the item renderer receives them whole.
rows.value: The controlled selection: one option object, or an array when multiple.
rows.filter: The built-in string filter. Pass null when filtering happens server-side.
rows.itemToStringLabel: Extracts the searchable string from an option — typeahead reads it.
rows.anchor: Anchors the popup to a wrapper element instead of the trigger, so its width follows the field.

input.title: Input
input.description: A text field that accepts free-form input. Use the bare Input for simple values and wrap it in InputGroup when the field has an adornment — a leading icon, a trailing action button, or a label that clarifies the format.

variants.title: Sizes
variants.description: The default 36 px height is the product baseline for every control. The compact 32 px variant is for dense interfaces such as the calendar header toolbar.

states.title: States
states.description: Disabled, active with a value, and invalid (aria-invalid) — the three states a field can be in without being focused.

inputGroup.title: InputGroup — adorned input
inputGroup.description: An Input wrapped in InputGroup gains adornments without breaking the field rhythm. The leading adornment clarifies what to type; the trailing one carries an action or a unit.

usage.title: Real usage
usage.description: Input and InputGroup together cover the password field, the date picker popover, the combobox search, and every other text field in the product — linked through FormTextField, never written by hand.

api.title: API reference
api.description: Project-facing props on Input. Native input props and Base UI interaction props are forwarded unchanged. InputGroup has no styling props of its own.

default.label: Default · 36 px
default.description: The standard 36 px control for forms and settings screens.

sm.label: Compact · 32 px
sm.description: A 32 px field for toolbar inline inputs and dense table-row filters.

invalid.description: Invalid fields render the destructive ring and show validation feedback through FieldError — aria-invalid alone only paints the border.

icon.description: A leading icon clarifies the expected input. A clear button on the trailing edge keeps the layout stable.

email.description: A trailing icon hints at the format without getting in the way of typing.

button.description: A ghost button in the addon carries a discrete action next to the field. The small icon size keeps it level with the 36 px container.

text.description: A text label clarifies a fixed suffix like a domain or a unit.

password.title: Password toggle — as in FormPasswordField
password.description: An InputGroup with a trailing icon button that swaps between type="password" and type="text". The button uses size="icon-xs" to stay level with the 36 px container.

datePicker.title: Date picker — as in DatePicker
datePicker.description: An InputGroup with a calendar icon button that opens a popover calendar. The input accepts typed dates and the icon button opens the visual picker.

combobox.title: Search combobox — as in Combobox
combobox.description: An InputGroup with a leading search icon and a trailing badge. The same InputGroup shell holds the typed query and the popover toggle.

rows.size: Sets the control height: default (36 px) or sm (32 px).
rows.type: Passthrough to the native input type attribute (text, email, password, search, etc.).
rows.placeholder: Hint text shown in the field when empty.
rows.disabled: Prevents interaction and applies the disabled state with reduced opacity.
rows.invalid: Use aria-invalid to mark the field as having a validation error.

textarea.title: Textarea
textarea.description: A multi-line text field for notes and free-form content. It shares the control surface and focus style of Input, but grows vertically instead of horizontally. In the product it is used almost exclusively through FormTextareaField — a form wrapper that wires it to react-hook-form.

states.title: States
states.description: Disabled and invalid (aria-invalid) — the two states a textarea can be in without being focused.

rows.title: Rows and growing
rows.description: The textarea is sized by rows; field-sizing-content lets it grow with its content up to whatever ceiling the layout sets.

live.title: Live value
live.description: A controlled textarea shows the raw string it holds. auto-grow is opt-in via CSS (field-sizing-content) and needs no prop.

autoGrow.description: field-sizing-content makes the control grow with its content. No prop — it is the default class on the component.
autoGrow.sample: First line of notes that keeps growing as you type more content…

usage.title: Real usage
usage.description: Textarea lives in the product behind FormTextareaField (notes on entities) and inside InputGroupTextarea. It is never written by hand mark-up in business code.

wrapper.title: FormTextareaField — notes on entities
wrapper.description: The form wrapper wires the textarea to react-hook-form: value, onChange, onBlur and ref come from useController, and the error state flows through Field with aria-invalid on the control.
wrapper.label: Notes
wrapper.sample: Shared notes that everyone in the org can see…

group.title: InputGroupTextarea — a textarea with an adornment
group.description: InputGroup wraps a textarea with the same adornment slots as Input — for multi-line fields that carry a unit or an action.
group.sample: A multi-line field inside an InputGroup…

api.title: API reference
api.description: Project-facing props on the native textarea. rows and className are passthrough; the rest are native textarea attributes. field-sizing-content is a CSS behavior, not a prop.

invalid.description: Invalid textareas render the destructive ring; validation feedback flows through FieldError, not aria-invalid alone.

small.description: rows={2} with field-sizing-content — a short two-line field that can still grow.

default.description: rows={6} is the roomy default for a notes block.
default.sample:
Meeting notes from the design review.

Pin the follow-ups before the week is over.

rows.rows: Starting number of visible rows. The control grows when field-sizing-content applies.
rows.disabled: Prevents interaction and applies the disabled state.
rows.invalid: Use aria-invalid to mark the field as having a validation error.

select.title: Select
select.description: A dropdown list of mutually exclusive options. Values are always strings on the wire — numeric or enum fields convert at the call site. The popup opens below the trigger (alignItemWithTrigger is off by default, a local change).

variants.title: Sizes
variants.description: The default 36 px control is the product baseline. The compact 32 px variant is for dense toolbars and compact rows.

groups.title: Groups, labels, separators
groups.description: SelectGroup + SelectLabel + SelectSeparator build a sectioned popup — for option lists that benefit from a heading or a divider.

usage.title: Real usage
usage.description: Select appears in the calendar reminders row (numeric presets as strings), the week-start picker in calendar settings, and the owner filter in the inline-form stand. All three convert between the string wire format and their domain type on the spot.

calendarReminders.title: Reminder presets — as in ReminderRows
calendarReminders.description: A numeric select that maps minute values to human labels ("At start", "15 min"). The value stays a string; the number conversion happens in onValueChange.

weekStarts.title: First day of week — as in Settings → Calendar
weekStarts.description: A numeric select fed by the Date.getDay() format. Not FormSelect (which expects a string key) — the numeric conversion is done at the call site.

filterBar.title: Owner filter — as in the inline form
filterBar.description: A filter-bar select inside an InputGroup-free row; the trigger stretches with w-full and the popup matches its width.

interactivity.title: Interactivity
interactivity.description: Base UI keyboard navigation: Arrow keys move between items, Enter and Escape work as expected. The popup stays below the trigger (alignItemWithTrigger: false) so the chosen item never hides the field.
interactivity.hint: Click and use Arrow keys, Enter to select, Escape to close.

api.title: API reference
api.description: Project-facing styling props on SelectTrigger. Root, Value, Item and the popup forward Base UI's props unchanged.

default.description: The default 36 px trigger — for forms and settings.

sm.description: The compact 32 px trigger — for toolbars and dense rows.

rows.size: Sets the control height: default (36 px) or sm (32 px).
rows.value: The currently selected value, a string. Pass null for an empty selection.
rows.onValueChange: Called with the new value (string) or null when the selection clears.
rows.items: Shortcut for a plain list of { value, label } items values.
rows.disabled: Prevents interaction and applies the disabled state.

tabs.title: Tabs
tabs.description: Tabs switch between sibling views of the same screen. Their visual weight should match how much room they share with the controls around them.

variants.title: Variants
variants.description: The default segment surface suits a standalone control block. The line variant reads as a lighter, text-first switch and needs no trough of its own.

sizes.title: Sizes
sizes.description: The default 36 px trough is the product baseline. The compact 32 px trough is for a control that has to sit level with other 32 px controls, such as a toolbar.

usage.title: Real usage
usage.description: Two shapes already live in the product: a default-size control that owns a content panel per tab, and a compact controlled switch with no content of its own.

api.title: API reference
api.description: Project-facing styling props on TabsList. Root, Tab, and Panel forward Base UI's Tabs props unchanged.

default.label: Default
default.description: A segment surface: the active tab sits on a raised tile (inverted to near-white in dark mode).

line.label: Line
line.description: An underline indicator on transparent ground — no trough.

content.title: Content tabs — as on the customer card
content.description: defaultValue plus TabsContent: each tab owns a panel, and the trough is the default 36 px size.

switcher.title: View switcher — as in the calendar header
switcher.description: A controlled value/onValueChange pair with no TabsContent at all: the page below renders the view itself, and the compact size keeps the control level with its neighbours in the header row.

rows.variant: Selects the trough style: default (segment) or line (underline).
rows.size: Sets the trough height and typography: default or sm.
rows.orientation: Root prop, forwarded from Base UI unchanged — horizontal (default) or vertical.

userSelect.title: Multi user select
userSelect.description: Two layouts for picking several users. Both share one data source — server-side search over active users of the tenant — and one popup; only the container differs.

inline.title: Inline — chips in the field
inline.description: Keeps the 36 px control rhythm of the surrounding form. The search caret lives in the field, so Backspace on an empty field drops the last chip.
inline.hint: Best while the list stays short: six users already wrap the field onto three rows.

stacked.title: Stacked — a list of rows
stacked.description: Each row has a right edge, so it can carry per-user state a chip has no room for. Empty state is a single dashed slot the size of a row.
stacked.hint: The first user added stands in for the organiser: no remove, no grip, pinned first. The round dot is anything that would not fit on a 48 px row.

userSelect.commentSample: Joining from the road — I might be ten minutes late to the call.

dialog.title: Dialog scroll
dialog.description: A modal is the only place where a scroller is born from a compromise — a height ceiling, a pinned header and footer, and content of unknown length all at once. These stands show the shape that survives both extremes.

long.title: Tall dialog
long.description: Content taller than the ceiling: the body scrolls, the header and footer stay put, and the overlay scrollbar takes no width from the fields.
long.heading: Edit preferences

short.title: Short dialog, same markup
short.description: Identical markup and the same max-height: the dialog must stay as tall as its content. If the scroller stretched itself, the ceiling would become a fixed height.
short.heading: Rename
short.name: Name
short.hint: Shown to everyone in your organization.

verticalForm.title: Vertical form
verticalForm.description: The product default: one column, the label above its control, and a width set by how far the eye can track a line — not by the width of the screen. New form components land here first, because this is where they will spend most of their life.
verticalForm.startHint: Type it or pick it: the field shows {{mask}} and accepts several looser shapes.

live.title: A live form
live.description: Wired to react-hook-form and a Zod schema, not drawn. Due date is bounded by start date, so the pair shows both the calendar limit and the schema message. Submit prints what the form actually holds.

inlineForm.title: Inline form
inlineForm.description: Several fields on one row plus an action: the filter bar above a list, a report parameter strip, a quick-create row. A row is stricter than a column in two ways, and both are on trial here — a field needs a sensible width of its own, and it has to survive wrapping without scattering its labels.

labelled.title: Labelled row
labelled.description: Labels stay above their controls, the row wraps as a whole. Fields grow from a basis rather than a fixed width, so extra space goes to whoever needs it.

toolbar.title: Toolbar without labels
toolbar.description: Denser, and the whole burden of explaining a field falls on its placeholder. This is where the date mask earns its keep: mm/dd/yyyy reads as an instruction, an example date would read as a value already entered.

narrow.title: Wrapping
narrow.description: The same row inside a narrow container. Nothing here should clip, overflow, or drop its label — the popup calendar still opens against the field, not the container.

beside.title: Label beside the control
beside.description: Field orientation="horizontal" — the settings-row shape. Not a form-per-row layout, but the closest relative of one, so it belongs on this stand.

datePicker.title: Date picker
datePicker.description: A typeable field with a calendar in a popover. Typing is the primary path — someone who knows the date enters it faster than they can scroll a grid to it, and a plain input is easier on a screen reader than forty-two buttons. The calendar is the second path, for dates you do not know yet.

tiles.iso: The skeleton default: the field shows exactly what the value holds. Unambiguous, same width in every language, and identical to what ships on the wire.
tiles.long: A longer label where the date is the point of the screen. Set in code, per screen — never a user setting.
tiles.label: A plain month caption instead of dropdowns — for dates that live near today.
tiles.past: max stops the calendar at today. Useful for a birthday or a past-only date.
tiles.disabled: Read-only: the same form, without the right to change it.
tiles.invalid: The error state comes from aria-invalid, exactly like every other control.

accepts.title: What the field accepts from the keyboard
accepts.description: The field reads far more than it writes. Order and separators for the locale-specific shapes come from Intl, so nothing here is a hardcoded English format. Type into any field above and leave it to see the result.
accepts.iso: Always accepted — and, being the default display format, what the field gives back.
accepts.localeOrder: Numbers in the order of the current locale (month first in en-US, day first almost everywhere else).
accepts.noYear: No year: the current one is used.
accepts.dayOnly: A day in the current month.
accepts.compact: Eight digits in a row, yyyymmdd.
accepts.namedMonth: Month by name, full or short, in any position.
accepts.invalid: Not a date: the field silently returns to its last valid value.

dataGrid.subtitle: Mock invoices — 50 rows × 32 fields to exercise field sets, the field panel and column reordering.
